browser_proof.clip: row 7 (02:08-02:10), clips/segment_0008.mp4 from the fresh 2026-07-18 focused run
browser_proof.observed: 2 LIVE_PROVISIONAL overlays (live:track_1@0.00, live:track_2@0.00) with dashed styling and YOLO TRACK_1/TRACK_2 labels; badge 'LIVE TRACKER DONE: 2 PROVISIONAL BOXES (10 EVENTS, LIVE_STREAM_COMPLETE)'

does_not_prove: overlay alignment over decoded video pixels (blocked by machine media decode)
identity promotion from live labels (by design, still forbidden)
proves: the Watch UI consumes live SSE track_update events from a spawned YOLO/ByteTrack run
provisional overlays render with live status and per-track labels, gated to PROVISIONAL only
overlay geometry works without decoded video metadata

environment_caveat: Browser media decode was broken machine-wide during this proof (Chrome's native player spins on any mp4, including a synthetic testsrc clip; likely the outdated NVIDIA driver). Video pixels therefore render black. The live overlay path was made decode-independent (SSE meta dimensions) — which is the correct design for RTSP sources that are never browser-playable. Overlay-over-decoded-video composition should be re-screenshotted once the driver is updated.
flow: Watch clip modal 'Live track' toggle opens EventSource to /api/projects/watch/tracker-events/stream?mode=live
server spawns track_yolo_bytetrack.py --stdout-jsonl (now incremental per-event emission) via the skill venv python
SSE meta event carries ffprobe-derived source_width/source_height so overlay geometry does not depend on browser media decode
track_update events accumulate client-side; nearest event per track within 0.45s of the playhead renders as a dashed amber LIVE_PROVISIONAL overlay with track label
status badge reports live tracker state, provisional box count, event count, and completion status
gate: UI live-event consumption (next gate after P0A/P0B per streaming sequence)
